### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **39** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/api.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**22** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fa494d0538fe69e19be4a21ab13b92e8e6ae8d23`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/api.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `created_at (literal, 42 pages)`, `/data/{child} (route, 60 pages)`, `/data/{object} (route, 75 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fa494d0538fe69e19be4a21ab13b92e8e6ae8d23` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `dc5eb91a85dbfd27385f1ccabf748b0f703b3d0e` — the merge of head `3b6fec5285b7b84331947ae2750103972241ac43` into base `fa494d0538fe69e19be4a21ab13b92e8e6ae8d23`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin dc5eb91a85dbfd27385f1ccabf748b0f703b3d0e && git checkout dc5eb91a85dbfd27385f1ccabf748b0f703b3d0e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin fa494d0538fe69e19be4a21ab13b92e8e6ae8d23 3b6fec5285b7b84331947ae2750103972241ac43 && git checkout -B drift-repro fa494d0538fe69e19be4a21ab13b92e8e6ae8d23 && git merge --no-ff 3b6fec5285b7b84331947ae2750103972241ac43

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fa494d0538fe69e19be4a21ab13b92e8e6ae8d23
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs fa494d0538fe69e19be4a21ab13b92e8e6ae8d23` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

The commit-status API reports `pending` with zero statuses, which is the empty default, not a pending check. All of them belong to this PR's head.

PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no login note is owed.

### ① Derived judgments

Request, `RecordPageRequestSchema` (still `.strict()`, the query-parameter set still empty):

- `related[].expand?: string[]` (each `min(1)`, no array cap). Named right. The route lowers it to the relation map `{ rel: { object: rel } }`, the same spelling the export route and the list normalizer use for `$expand=a,b`, so a list's rows expand as its own `GET /data/{child}?$expand=` read does. No cap on the array, as the record-level `expand` already has none. Consistent, noted.
- `discussion?: boolean`. Named right. A non-boolean is refused (spec and route tests).
- `activity?: { top: int 1..200 }`, strict. Named right. `min(1)` means a count-only activity part cannot be asked, where `attachments` allows `top: 0`. An asymmetry, not a defect: the console never asks a count alone here.
- `attachments?: { top: int 0..100 }`, strict. Named right; `0` is the count alone, as `related[].top` already reads.

Response, `RecordPageResponseSchema` (a non-strict object, as before):

- `discussion?: RecordPageDiscussionSchema | RecordPageStreamRefusalSchema`. Both arms strict, so a refused stream cannot parse as an empty one. `reactions` is its own union `{ records } | { error }`, so a deployment without `sys_comment_reaction` answers its 404 inside the part and the comments stay answered. Named right; the spec test pins "rows or refusal, never both, never neither" for all three parts.
- `activity?` and `attachments?`: `RecordPageStreamRowsSchema { total, records } | RecordPageStreamRefusalSchema`. Named right.
- `RecordPageStreamRefusalSchema` is `RecordPagePartErrorSchema` made strict. Two names for one shape; the strict copy is what makes the unions disjoint, so it earns its place.
- Each new response key appears only when the request asked for it. A request from an old client (no `discussion`, `activity`, `attachments`, no `related[].expand`) receives the pre-PR answer byte for byte: `record`, `related` rows with bare ids, the three optional parts as before. Kept.
- Order of the activity part: `timestamp desc` with `top`. The console's own read on `main` asked `asc` with `$top: 200`. For a record with more than 200 rows the payload now carries the newest 200 instead of the oldest 200, and the console's fallback read was changed to `desc` too. A deliberate change, documented in the stream table, and the right one for a feed. Noted.
- Discussion: `thread_id = {object}:{id}`, `created_at asc`, no page size. The console wrote and read exactly this thread id and sent no `$top`, and the engine applies no default limit to a `find` without one (engine comment: `limit` carries no `.default()`), so the part is the same read. See ③ and ④ for the size question.
- New exports: 6 schemas, 2 constants and their `X` / `XParsed` types, all listed in `api-surface/api.json` (20 lines) and `export-origins/api.json`. `authorable-surface/api.json` gains 14 `api/RecordPage*` keys; the os-dev-report wrote 17. The diff is 14. Prose only, the artifacts are generated and `check:generated` passed in CI.
- The spec module's header and the stream table on `RecordPageActivityRequestSchema` match the route line for line (filters, orders, `count`, `actor_id` expand). Named right.

### ② Semver level

- Declaration lines on the PR body and on `.changeset/28470-record-page-streams.md`: `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added`. They match the seat's amendment 6558547648 on the card. `added` is right: 14 new authorable keys enter the `api` shard, nothing existing moves meaning.
- `@objectstack/spec: minor`. Right for `added`.
- `@objectstack/rest: patch` in the same changeset. AGENTS.md rule 3 reads "a kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves". `check-changeset-no-major` mechanizes the softer form "at least one moved package `minor`+" and passed. The route gains four new accepted body members and three new answer members, an additive feature on a published package, and #27713, which opened this very door, graded `@objectstack/rest` `minor` under the same kind. **Should-fix:** lift `@objectstack/rest` to `minor`, or have the seat record that the gate's "at least one" reading governs over the rule text. Not a FAIL: the gate accepted it and the published behaviour is unaffected.
- `.changeset/28470-console-record-open-one-request.md`: four `@object-ui/*` packages at `patch` under `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. Consistent with its own line: no metadata key moves there, and `RecordPagePayload` is a TypeScript type for console consumers, not an authorable protocol. The two changesets carry different `Metadata-protocol` lines; the PR body carries the stronger one, which is what the gate reads. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations, from the os-dev-report (card comment 6558534355) and the PR body:

1. Declaration lines versus the changeset gate. Answered: the seat amended the claim to `Metadata-protocol: added`, `@objectstack/spec` `minor` (card comment 6558547648); commit `579bcda1` carries it; `Check Changeset` is green on the head.
2. The activity part asks 200 rows, where the card said "at the size the 动态 panel draws, not 200". Named in the report, the PR body and the schema constant's docblock. The reason holds: the 动态 count chip and tab count the merged stream client-side over the rows held, so a 5-row window would make the count wrong. The deviation is accepted as named. **Should-fix:** file the class-b out-of-scope finding (a server-side count of the merged stream) as a card before landing, so `RECORD_PAGE_MAX_ACTIVITY_ROWS = 200` has an owner; shrinking that cap later is a narrowing and needs its own review.
3. Files touched beyond the amended surface: `RecordAttachmentsPanel.tsx` and four test files. `RecordAttachmentsPanel.tsx` is in the original claim's file surface (card comment 6556969643), so it is in surface; the tests pin retired reads beside the files they test. Answered.
4. A reply or edit with an `@` before the composer was ever focused reads the roster at the write. Right: without it a mention would resolve to nobody once the open stopped reading `sys_user`. Pinned in `withheldMentions-28218`. Answered.
5. No assignees or reviewers on the PR. Process, per the seat's rules. Answered.

`open_questions`: one, "amend `Metadata-protocol` to `added` or accept the red". Answered by the seat's amendment 6558547648 and carried on the head.

Flags the report did not raise:

6. The discussion part is the whole thread with no page size. The card's Target 1 asked for "the first page of the discussion". The dev matched the console's existing unbounded read (parity, see ①) but did not name the gap. **Should-fix:** name it in the PR body's Deviations with the reason (the feed draws the whole thread and has no paging door today), so the card's wording and the shipped contract agree on record.
7. Acceptance 3 asked for before and after lists on HotCRM contact John Smith. The PR measured `examples/app-crm` on a production build and says HotCRM was not available. The lists are complete (URLs, counts, the request body) and the card's own Measured section names app-crm as the same shape. Accepted as named; the epic seat's preview check (Acceptance 4) is still outstanding and is not this review's.
8. Card item 4 (`/page` twice): measured once per open on a production build; the other posts are the prev/next prefetch. Answered as the card prescribed ("record that in the PR and change nothing").

### ④ Design judgment

The hit file is judged against the card's Wanted list, #27627's rule "every part is the read it replaces, as the same caller", and its first consumer, the console's `RecordDetailView`.

Read authority. The route reads the record first through `getData` as the caller; its refusal is the whole answer before any stream is asked (the dogfood pins `page` equal to the member's own `GET` 404, byte for byte). Each stream is `findData` over its own object with the caller's `context`, after `apiAccessDenialFromEnable(item.enable, name, 'list')`, which is the same verdict `enforceApiAccess('list')` renders on `GET /data/{object}` (the extra API-key credential check there applies to writes on `sys_api_key` only). A stream object the deployment does not have throws `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` into the part's refusal, as the list door 404s it. Row-level and field-level security are the engine's, applied inside `findData` as on the `GET`. The dogfood test compares the member's part against the member's own `GET` reads, rows and `total` included, and asserts another record's attachments are neither counted nor listed. The filters are pinned to the route's own `{object}` and `{id}`, which the record read has just proven readable, so a stream cannot be aimed at another record. The reactions read is scoped to the comment ids the caller just received. I find no way the payload reads a row the caller's scope refuses on the data door.

`related[].expand` and read authority. The engine's expand sub-read re-enters the security middleware for the referenced object with the full treatment (CRUD gate, `requiredPermissions`, RLS, FLS, since #7626), and a refusal leaves the bare id in place. So the rows carry only referenced records the caller could read directly, which is what the schema's description promises. The API exposure flag of the referenced object (`enable.apiEnabled`) is not consulted on an expansion, but that is the published behaviour of `GET /data/{child}?$expand=` today, so the payload opens no door the list door did not already hold. Not a widening of read authority. Noted so the next reviewer of the expand path knows where the line sits.

The approvals door. #28546 and #28657 were the same class, an approvals row read through a generic data-scoped door. This PR does not touch that line: `RecordDetailView` still asks no payload for `sys_approval_request`, and the routed source still refuses `getRecordPage` for it. The new parts ride only a payload the plan already asks, so a request page asks none of them. Right.

Per-part refusal. A refused activity read leaves the record, the discussion, the attachments and the related lists answered (route test and console test, `data-denied-source="activity"`). A refused comment read refuses the discussion alone and asks no reaction read. A refused reaction read keeps the comments. The three unions are disjoint by strictness, so no consumer can read a refusal as an empty stream. Holds.

Response size. Per open the payload now carries up to 200 activity rows with the actor expanded, up to 100 attachment rows, the whole comment thread and its reactions, plus every related list's rows with their lookups expanded. These are the same bytes the console fetched in separate requests before; the one body is the card's point. The one unbounded term is the thread (flag 6). The neighbour prefetch now asks the same streams for the previous and next records, so a drawer open reads three records' streams rather than one. That is a console cost decision outside the hit file; recorded here for the epic seat's preview check, not a finding.

Stale counts against the related-list filter. The attachments `total` is seeded into `RelatedCountStore` under the key the Attachments tab badge probes (`attachments:{object}`, filter `undefined`), and the badge's probe wrapper injects the same two-key scope `{ parent_object, parent_id }` the route filters by, so badge and panel answer one question. `takeRows` hands the rows over only when the seeded `top` covers the panel's `limit` (100 against 100) and the order matches (`undefined` on both). After an upload, a delete or Retry the panel reads for itself. A related list's `total` is unchanged by this PR; `expand` touches rows only. Holds.

Strictness. The body is strict at every level; a window past its cap, an undeclared key in a part, a non-boolean flag and a non-array `expand` are each a 400 before any read (route and spec tests). The query-parameter set is still empty.

The first consumer. The console asks `discussion` and `activity` only when a feed block is on screen at open and `attachments` only when the page draws them; the parts are taken off the payload once and never re-read on the open; a part the payload did not carry is read as before. The mention roster moves to the composer's first focus. The one-request test asserts one `/page` and zero `sys_comment`, `sys_comment_reaction`, `sys_activity`, `sys_attachment`, `sys_user?top=50` and `?top=1` reads, with two ablations that make the detectors fire. Acceptance 1 and 2 of the card are met by tests on the head.

No must-fix. Three should-fixes: ② the `@objectstack/rest` level, ③-2 the follow-up card for the 200-row cap, ③-6 the unnamed whole-thread deviation.
